facts.fact: The civic palace remains a seat of municipal administration and developed through several building phases from the late thirteenth century. Its two principal facades face Piazza IV Novembre and Corso Vannucci.
facts.location: Main introduction and “Multiple buildings, one single heart for governing the city”.

facts.fact: The palace contains the Sala dei Notari and the National Gallery of Umbria. Its civic, gallery and guild spaces are distinct parts of the building, not one undifferentiated public interior.
facts.location: Historical account and “The façade on the main street”.

facts.fact: The square-side portal displays bronze copies of the Griffin and Guelph Lion; their originals are housed in the palace atrium. The facade includes grouped lancet windows.
facts.excerpt: the originals are housed in the palace atrium
facts.location: “The façade on the square: between ancient symbols and public functions”, second paragraph; opening description.
